claim: The default proxy endpoint for a Multi-AZ DB cluster is read/write and sends all requests to the writer; only for a proxy associated with a Multi-AZ DB cluster can you add read/write or read-only endpoints, and a read-only endpoint spreads read queries over the readers.
question: Can RDS Proxy provide a read-only endpoint, and for which deployments?

values.display: sends all requests to the writer instance

qualifiers.scope: RDS Proxy with Multi-AZ DB clusters
qualifiers.condition: the proxy is associated with a Multi-AZ DB cluster

evidence.quote: By default, the endpoint that you connect to when you use RDS Proxy with a Multi-AZ DB cluster has read/write capability. As a result, this endpoint sends all requests to the writer instance of the cluster. All of those connections count against the `max_connections` value for the writer instance. If your proxy is associated with a Multi-AZ DB cluster, then you can create additional read/write or read-only endpoints for that proxy.
For RDS DB clusters, you can also create additional read/write and read-only endpoints.

claim: Back-end connections are reused only for clients with the same database user name, so many unique database accounts (for example one per tenant) fragment the pool into micro-pools and reduce RDS Proxy's efficiency.
question: When does RDS Proxy give little benefit because of how clients log in?

evidence.quote: This behavior can significantly reduce pooling and multiplexing efficiency in multi-user environments with a large number of unique database accounts.

If the database contains a thousand schemas (one per tenant) and each tenant connects to the database with a different user name, the connection pool becomes fragmented into user-specific micro-pools, reducing overall efficiency.
